# Best RV power station and solar combo

For an RV, check three things: a 30A RV outlet, enough output to start a roof air conditioner, and a solar input that matches your panels. A 13,500 BTU roof AC draws about 1,500W running and spikes past 3,000W at startup ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)). A 1,000W-class unit won't start it.

## My picks

**1. Full-time boondocking: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**
- It has 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous and 8,000W surge. It expands past 12kWh and recharges 0-80% in about 50 minutes from a wall outlet.
- It's heavy, a two-person lift, and the most expensive option once you add batteries.
- Source: [EmergencyEnergy RV comparison](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/). That site is Ontario-focused, so ignore its Canadian electrical-code notes. I didn't get a price or a direct store link.

**2. Best value with a built-in RV port: BLUETTI AC200L**
- It has 2,048Wh, 2,400W output and up to 1,200W of solar input. It weighs about 62 lb and has a built-in 30A RV outlet.
- Sources: [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) and [SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/).

**3. Most capacity per dollar: ALLPOWERS R4000**
- It has 3,456Wh of LiFePO4 and 3,600W at 120V (6,000W peak), plus an RV outlet. It accepts up to 2,000W of solar across three inputs, but each input maxes at 650W. It carries a 5-year warranty.
- It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it stays put in the RV.
- The price was $1,499, or $1,319.12 with code EXTRA12 when tested on 2026-10-23. Prices change, so confirm at checkout. Returns are 30 days for unused items, and you pay return shipping unless it's defective.
- [Buy at ALLPOWERS](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. Details: [Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh).

**Lighter weekend option: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 or 1000 Plus**
- It's simple and light (about 24 lb), but the v2 caps solar input at 400W and is a poor fit for running an AC ([SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).
- The Explorer 1000 Plus is called the best all-rounder for vanlife and Starlink-type loads in [NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife).

## Solar panels

- **Match the panels to the input limit.** Extra panels beyond the station's ceiling add nothing ([GetWattLogic](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life)).
- **Portable panels:** 300-400W of folding panels can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)). Brand-matched options include Jackery SolarSaga 100W/200W, EcoFlow panels, and the Renogy 200W foldable suitcase ([NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)).
- **Roof panels:** For a roof array on the AC200L or R4000, check the station's voltage and current limits first. The R4000 takes 12-60V and 13A per input.

## Quick sizing

- A fridge at about 150W for 10 hours is about 1,500Wh ([Acquired Sense](https://www.acquiredsense.com/reviews/power-stations.html)).
- If you'll run the AC off-grid, go with the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3, Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro or ALLPOWERS R4000.
- For lights, a fridge, a laptop and Starlink, 1,000-2,000Wh is enough.

I couldn't verify current prices for the EcoFlow, BLUETTI or Jackery models, and the sources disagree on some specs. Tell me your AC use, trip length and budget, and I can narrow it down and look for direct buy links and bundle prices.
